title: Equivariant Polynomials for Graph Neural Networks

en.text: If you want to say how powerful a graph neural network (GNN) is, the field's standard answer is the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) hierarchy, a family of graph-isomorphism tests. The higher a model sits in the hierarchy, the more graphs it can tell apart, and the more expressive it is presumed to be. WL has become the default vocabulary for talking about GNN expressive power, cited across a huge swath of the literature.

But WL is an awkward ruler in two ways. First, its definition is combinatorial: it tells you which rung a model is stuck on, but not what operation it is missing or what to add to climb higher. For anyone trying to improve a model, that is almost no guidance at all. Second, its gradations are coarse. Many modern GNNs with very different architectures land on the same WL rung, so the test simply cannot separate them.

This ICML 2023 paper swaps the ruler. Instead of asking which isomorphism test a model passes, it asks which equivariant graph polynomials the model can compute. An equivariant polynomial is a polynomial in the adjacency matrix that respects node relabeling, and it is a natural target: subgraph counts and many structural features are exactly such polynomials. The higher the degree a model can compute, the stronger it is, and the polynomials it cannot yet compute form a concrete to-do list of the operations it lacks.

en.caption: Figure 1. Two example basis elements of equivariant graph polynomials: node-valued (top) and edge-valued (bottom). Each basis element is a small directed multi-graph carrying one special (red) edge, and evaluating it on a graph is a single tensor contraction (an einsum). This is the paper's central intuition: a polynomial is just a small graph.

en.text: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11556
Code: https://github.com/omri1348/Equivariant-Polynomaials
The problem: why WL is not enough

A GNN's expressive power is, at bottom, the set of functions of a graph it can represent, and that set is bounded: no matter how many layers you stack, a standard message-passing network cannot separate certain non-isomorphic graphs. WL characterizes this bound, but as noted it is neither constructive nor fine-grained. What the authors want instead is a ruler that both separates today's models and points directly at the operations a weak model is missing.

Earlier work had only characterized very low-degree equivariant maps, or leaned on WL, leaving a gap: a complete, computation-friendly description of what a GNN should be able to output. Filling that gap is the paper's starting point.
Contribution one: a complete basis, where every element is a multi-graph

The first contribution is a complete basis for all equivariant graph polynomials of degree at most d. Theorem 2.1 states that this basis is enumerated by directed multi-graphs H = (V, E, (a, b)), with |V| ≤ min{n, 2+2d}, |E| ≤ d, and (a, b) a marked (red) edge. In other words, the abstract space of equivariant polynomials is put into one-to-one correspondence with a collection of small graphs.

And how is each basis element evaluated on a graph? By a single tensor contraction, the einsum expression familiar from deep learning: multiply entries of the adjacency matrix along the black edges of H, then sum over the internal nodes. The simplest example of this is something everyone already knows: ordinary matrix multiplication.

en.caption: Figure 2. Matrix multiplication XY expressed as a tensor contraction: three nodes, two black edges, and one red output edge, whose einsum is exactly the product XY. The takeaway is that the paper's tensor contractions are nothing exotic; they are just familiar graph linear algebra rewritten in the language of multi-graphs.

en.text: How does the construction guarantee equivariance? The authors average an ordinary monomial over all node permutations using the Reynolds operator, and then show that this average equals a sum over the orbit of H, that is, over all the isomorphic copies of H obtained under permutation. Building an equivariant polynomial thus reduces to enumerating a multi-graph's orbit, a purely combinatorial task.

en.caption: Figure 3. The complete basis of constant (left of the bold line) and linear (right of the bold line) equivariant graph polynomials. Each cell is a small multi-graph, with the red edge marking the output slot. Together the grid is an exhaustive inventory of the low-degree space: every equivariant constant or linear map is a linear combination of these elements.

en.text: Contribution two: a linear-time test for a model's polynomial power

With a basis in hand, one can ask a very concrete question: given a GNN, which of these polynomials can it actually compute? The second contribution treats a network as a bank of primitive contractions F, and gives an algorithm (Algorithm 1) that decides, in time linear in |V| and |E|, whether a target polynomial can be assembled by repeatedly contracting nodes.

Applying this tool, the authors tabulate the polynomial power of standard GNNs, and two clean results fall out. A bank that only allows node contractions, F_n, turns out to equal 1-WL exactly; a stronger bank that also allows edge contractions, F_e, equals 2-FWL (better known as 3-WL). The figure below draws the primitive building blocks of both banks.

en.caption: Figure 4 (paper Figure 7). The prototypical node-based (left) and edge-based (right) contraction banks; gray nodes are the ones being contracted. The node-based bank F_n corresponds to 1-WL, and the edge-based bank F_e corresponds to 2-FWL (3-WL). The extra primitives on the edge side are precisely what make it stronger.

en.text: This is not a paper exercise. Table 1 quantifies it: on degree-3 polynomials the edge-based model F_e leaves only 0 of 18 basis elements non-computable, whereas the node-based F_n leaves 2 of 8, matching the fact that F_e is 5-node- and 4-edge-polynomial-exact while F_n reaches only 2-node-polynomial-exact.
Contribution three: turning the theory into a model, PPGN++ and precomputed features

Since the theory now says which polynomials are missing, the natural third step is to supply them. On top of the powerful matrix-multiplication network (PPGN/Ring-GNN), the authors do two things. They replace the bloated design that needs separate parameters for each of the 15 linear basis elements with a small set of primitive operations, yielding a leaner, more efficient backbone they call PPGN++. And they precompute high-degree equivariant polynomial features and feed them straight into the network.

That second move is the crux. The polynomial features already encode structure that 3-WL cannot see, and because they are precomputed, the network gains expressive power that is provably strictly beyond 3-WL at almost no runtime cost. Experiments: state of the art on molecules, past 3-WL on SR graphs

The evaluation spans two settings. For real-world performance, the authors use three standard molecular graph regression datasets: ZINC-12K (about twelve thousand molecules), the larger ZINC-full (over two hundred thousand), and Alchemy, all measured by test mean absolute error (MAE, lower is better), with every model held to a 500K parameter budget following Dwivedi et al. (2020) and Lim et al. (2022). For raw expressive power they use Strongly Regular (SR) graphs, families notoriously hard to tell apart that 3-WL cannot separate at all, measuring the failure rate at distinguishing non-isomorphic pairs.

en.caption: Table 1. Test MAE on three molecular graph regression benchmarks (lower is better, all within a 500K parameter budget). PPGN++ with degree-6 polynomial features is best in class on all three.

en.text: PPGN++ with degree-6 polynomial features takes the top spot on all three: 0.071 on ZINC-12K (versus 0.079 for CIN and 0.163 for GIN), 0.020 on ZINC-full, and 0.109 on Alchemy. Just as striking, the features are model-agnostic. Bolting degree-6 features onto a plain GatedGCN backbone cuts its ZINC-12K MAE from 0.265 to 0.106, so the benefit does not hinge on any one architecture.

Feature degree matters too, and monotonically. On ZINC-12K the base model scores 0.076, degree-5 features bring it to 0.072, and degree-6 to 0.071. On the SR graphs the same trend is far more dramatic.

en.caption: Figure 5 (paper Figure 10). Failure rate at distinguishing non-isomorphic SR graph pairs, by family (log scale, lower is better). For both the GatedGCN and PPGN backbones, adding polynomial features drives the failure rate down by orders of magnitude as the degree climbs from 5 to 7, while 3-WL fails on these graphs entirely. This is direct evidence that precomputed polynomial features push the model past the 3-WL barrier.

en.text: Takeaway: making "how expressive?" a checkable, actionable question

The lasting contribution here is turning a vague question, "how expressive is this GNN?", into a concrete and checkable one: "which equivariant graph polynomials can it compute?" Every such polynomial is just a small multi-graph evaluated by a tensor contraction, which gives both a finer ruler than WL and an explicit, itemized list of exactly which operations a given model still lacks and could be extended to include.

Acting on that list, the authors use precomputed polynomial features to push ordinary graph networks past the 3-WL barrier and to state-of-the-art accuracy on molecular property prediction, all within a modest 500K parameter budget. They are candid about what comes next, including working with a generating set of polynomials rather than the full basis to reduce how many features the network ingests, and incorporating currently-uncomputable polynomials as in-layer computational primitives rather than as precomputed features. For anyone working on graph learning, the paper turns "make the model stronger" from guesswork into a concrete engineering task with an actual checklist to work through.

It is worth being precise about the cost. Because the polynomial features are precomputed once, before training, and passed in as extra inputs, the gain in expressive power does not turn into a heavier per-step runtime, and every model reported in the paper still fits inside the same 500K parameter budget as its baselines. Paired with the linear-time computability algorithm, this is what lets the central question, whether a given network can compute a given polynomial, become something a practitioner can check directly and then act on, instead of a property that can only ever be argued about at the level of intuition and worst-case examples.

zh.text: 衡量一个图神经网络（GNN）到底“有多强”，长期以来的标准答案是 Weisfeiler-Lehman（WL）层级，一族用来判定图是否同构的测试。一个模型在 WL 层级里的位置越高，它能区分的图就越多，理论上也就越强。这套尺子被大量论文引用，几乎成了讨论 GNN 表达能力时的默认语言。
但 WL 这把尺子有两个让人别扭的地方。第一，它的定义是组合式的，只会告诉你“这个模型卡在第几级”，却不会告诉你“缺了哪一步、加上什么才能更强”，对想改进模型的人几乎没有可操作的指导。第二，它的刻度太粗：许多结构差别很大的现代 GNN，落在 WL 层级里却是同一级，根本分不开。
这篇 ICML 2023 的论文换了一把尺子。作者提出：不要问模型“通过了哪一级同构测试”，而要问它“能算出哪些图的等变多项式（equivariant polynomial）”。这里的等变多项式，指那些对节点重新编号保持一致的邻接矩阵多项式，子图计数、许多结构特征都恰好是这样的多项式。谁能算的多项式次数越高，谁就越强，而“还差哪个多项式”正好就是一张可执行的待办清单。

zh.caption: 图1 两个等变图多项式基元的例子：上方为节点值（node-valued），下方为边值（edge-valued）。每个基元都对应一个带一条红色特殊边的小多重图（multi-graph），在图上取值就等于按这个多重图做一次张量收缩（einsum）。这张图是全文的核心直觉：一个“多项式”其实就是一个小图。

zh.text: 论文地址：https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.11556
代码地址：https://github.com/omri1348/Equivariant-Polynomaials
问题：WL 层级为什么不够用
GNN 的表达能力，说白了就是“它能表示哪些关于图的函数”。这一点是有上界的：无论怎么堆层数，标准的消息传递网络都无法区分某些非同构的图。学界用 WL 层级来刻画这个上界，但正如前面所说，它既不构造、又太粗。作者想要的是一把既能细分现有模型、又能直接指出“该补什么运算”的尺子。
在此之前，已有工作只刻画了很低次（low-degree）的等变映射，或者仍然依赖 WL，缺一个完整且便于计算的描述：一个 GNN 到底“应该”能输出哪些量。这篇论文补上的正是这块拼图。
方法一：等变多项式的完整基，每个基元就是一个多重图
论文的第一个贡献，是给出了所有次数不超过 d 的等变图多项式的一组完整基。定理 2.1 说：这组基可以用有向多重图 H = (V, E, (a, b)) 来枚举，其中顶点数 |V| ≤ min{n, 2+2d}、边数 |E| ≤ d，(a, b) 是一条被标成红色的特殊边。换句话说，“等变多项式”这个抽象空间，被一一对应地翻译成了“一批小图”。
更关键的是，每个基元在图上怎么取值？答案是一次张量收缩，也就是深度学习里熟悉的 einsum：按 H 的每条黑边把邻接矩阵的元素相乘，再对内部节点求和。下面这张最简单的例子，就是我们再熟悉不过的矩阵乘法。

zh.caption: 图2 矩阵乘法 XY 作为一次张量收缩的例子：三个节点、两条黑边加一条红色输出边，对应的 einsum 恰好就是 (XY) 这个矩阵乘积。这说明作者所谓的“张量收缩”并不神秘，它就是把常见的图上线性代数运算统一写成了多重图的语言。

zh.text: 怎么保证这些多项式是等变的？作者用 Reynolds 算子（Reynolds operator）把普通的单项式在所有节点置换上做平均。论文进一步证明，这个平均恰好等于对 H 的轨道（orbit，即 H 在所有置换下得到的所有同构副本）求和。于是“构造一个等变多项式”这件事，被化简成了“枚举一个多重图的轨道”这件纯组合的事情。

zh.caption: 图3 常数（粗竖线左侧）与线性（粗竖线右侧）等变图多项式的完整基：每个格子里都是一个小多重图，红色边标出输出的位置。整张表就是低次等变多项式空间的一份“完整清单”，任何等变的常数或线性映射都是这些基元的线性组合。

zh.text: 方法二：一个线性时间算法，读出模型的“多项式功力”
有了基，就能问一个非常具体的问题：给定一个 GNN，它到底能算出上面哪些多项式？论文的第二个贡献，是把一个网络看成一“套”原始收缩操作（contraction bank）F，并给出一个在 |V|、|E| 上线性时间的算法（Algorithm 1），精确判定某个目标多项式能否被这套操作反复收缩组装出来。
用这套工具，作者把常见 GNN 的表达能力做成了一张对照表，并得到两个漂亮的结论：只允许“节点收缩”的操作集 F_n 恰好等价于 1-WL；允许“边收缩”的更强操作集 F_e 恰好等价于 2-FWL（也就是常说的 3-WL）。下图把这两套操作的原始积木画了出来。

zh.caption: 图4（论文 Figure 7）原型化的节点型（左）与边型（右）收缩操作库：灰色节点表示被收缩掉的节点。节点型操作库 F_n 对应 1-WL，边型操作库 F_e 对应 2-FWL（3-WL）。边型多出的几个积木，正是它比节点型更强的来源。

zh.text: 这张对照表不是纸面练习。论文的 Table 1 给出了量化：在 3 次多项式上，边型模型 F_e 只有 0/18 个基元算不出来，而节点型 F_n 有 2/8 个算不出来，直观印证了 F_e 是 5 节点、4 边多项式精确的，而 F_n 只到 2 节点多项式精确。
方法三：把理论变成模型，PPGN++ 与预计算多项式特征
既然理论已经指出“还差哪些多项式”，第三步自然就是去补。作者在强大的矩阵乘法网络（PPGN/Ring-GNN）基础上做了两件事：一是用一小组“原始”运算替换掉原来需要为全部 15 个线性基元分别配置参数的臃肿设计，得到一个更精简高效的骨干，称为 PPGN++；二是把高次的等变多项式特征预先算好（precomputed polynomial features），直接喂给网络。
第二点是点睛之笔。这些多项式特征本身就编码了 3-WL 无法捕捉的结构信息，而且因为是预计算的，网络在几乎不增加运行开销的前提下，表达能力被证明严格超过了 3-WL。PPGN++ 的单层更新写成如下形式，其中三个 m̄ 是可学习的原始运算，⊛ 表示逐元素乘：
实验：分子基准全面刷新，SR 图上跨越 3-WL

作者在两类任务上验证。真实性能方面，用三个标准的分子图回归数据集：ZINC-12K（约一万二千个分子）、更大的 ZINC-full（二十多万个）和 Alchemy，指标是测试集平均绝对误差（MAE，越低越好），所有模型都严守 500K 参数预算，遵循 Dwivedi 等（2020）和 Lim 等（2022）的协议。表达能力方面，用强正则图（Strongly Regular graphs）这类出了名难区分、连 3-WL 都分不开的图，衡量区分非同构图对的失败率。

zh.caption: 表1 三个分子图回归基准上的测试集 MAE（越低越好，均在 500K 参数预算内）。带 degree-6 多项式特征的 PPGN++ 在三项上全部取得当前最好成绩。

zh.text: 三项基准的头名都由带 degree-6 多项式特征的 PPGN++ 拿下：ZINC-12K 上 0.071（对比 CIN 的 0.079、GIN 的 0.163），ZINC-full 上 0.020，Alchemy 上 0.109。更有意思的是，这些多项式特征是“即插即用”的：给一个普通的 GatedGCN 骨干加上 degree-6 特征，它在 ZINC-12K 上的 MAE 从 0.265 直接降到 0.106。也就是说，收益并不依赖某个特定架构。
特征的次数（degree）也确实越高越好。在 ZINC-12K 上，基础版为 0.076，加 degree-5 特征降到 0.072，加 degree-6 再降到 0.071，趋势单调。而在强正则图上，这个趋势更为剧烈。

zh.caption: 图5（论文 Figure 10）在各族强正则图上区分非同构图对的失败率（纵轴对数刻度，越低越好）。无论是 GatedGCN 还是 PPGN 骨干，一旦加入多项式特征，随着次数从 5 升到 7，失败率成数量级地下降；而 3-WL 本身对这些图完全无能为力。这直接印证了“预计算多项式特征把模型推过了 3-WL 屏障”。

zh.text: 小结：让“有多强”变成一个可检查、可执行的问题
这篇论文最持久的价值，是把一个含糊的问题“这个 GNN 有多强”变成了一个具体的问题“它能算出哪些等变图多项式”。每个这样的多项式都只是一个小多重图，取值就是一次张量收缩，于是我们既得到了一把比 WL 更细的尺子，也得到了一张“缺哪些运算”的清单。

顺着这张清单动手，作者用预计算的多项式特征把普通图网络推过了 3-WL 屏障，并在分子性质预测上取得了当前最好的精度，而这一切都在 500K 参数的适度预算内完成。作者也坦诚指出了后续方向，例如用一组“生成元”而非完整基来减少喂入网络的特征数量，以及把暂时不可计算的多项式作为层内的计算原语（而非预计算特征）来进一步提升表达能力。对做图学习的人来说，这项工作把“把模型改强”从玄学变成了一件有清单、可核对的工程。

GNN 的表达能力，说白了就是“它能表示哪些关于图的函数”。这一点是有上界的：无论怎么堆层数，标准的消息传递网络都无法区分某些非同构的图。学界用 WL 层级来刻画这个上界，但正如前面所说，它既不构造、又太粗。作者想要的是一把既能细分现有模型、又能直接指出“该补什么运算”的尺子。
在此之前，已有工作只刻画了很低次（low-degree）的等变映射，或者仍然依赖 WL，缺一个完整且便于计算的描述：一个 GNN 到底“应该”能输出哪些量。这篇论文补上的正是这块拼图。

en.title: A Finer Ruler for Graph Networks: Grade Them by the Polynomials They Compute
en.subtitle: An ICML 2023 paper from Weizmann, MIT, NVIDIA, and Meta gives a complete basis for equivariant graph polynomials, and uses it to build PPGN++, a new state of the art on molecular benchmarks.

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 换一把更细的尺子：用等变多项式衡量图神经网络的表达能力
zh.subtitle: Weizmann、MIT、NVIDIA 与 Meta 给出等变图多项式的完整基，并据此设计出刷新分子基准的 PPGN++

en.text: Contribution one: a complete basis, where every element is a multi-graph

The first contribution is a complete basis for all equivariant graph polynomials of degree at most d. Theorem 2.1 states that this basis is enumerated by directed multi-graphs H = (V, E, (a, b)), with |V| ≤ min{n, 2+2d}, |E| ≤ d, and (a, b) a marked (red) edge. In other words, the abstract space of equivariant polynomials is put into one-to-one correspondence with a collection of small graphs.

And how is each basis element evaluated on a graph? By a single tensor contraction, the einsum expression familiar from deep learning: multiply entries of the adjacency matrix along the black edges of H, then sum over the internal nodes. The simplest example of this is something everyone already knows: ordinary matrix multiplication.

en.caption: Figure 2. Matrix multiplication XY expressed as a tensor contraction: three nodes, two black edges, and one red output edge, whose einsum is exactly the product XY. The takeaway is that the paper's tensor contractions are nothing exotic; they are just familiar graph linear algebra rewritten in the language of multi-graphs.

en.text: How does the construction guarantee equivariance? The authors average an ordinary monomial over all node permutations using the Reynolds operator, and then show that this average equals a sum over the orbit of H, that is, over all the isomorphic copies of H obtained under permutation. Building an equivariant polynomial thus reduces to enumerating a multi-graph's orbit, a purely combinatorial task.

en.caption: Figure 3. The complete basis of constant (left of the bold line) and linear (right of the bold line) equivariant graph polynomials. Each cell is a small multi-graph, with the red edge marking the output slot. Together the grid is an exhaustive inventory of the low-degree space: every equivariant constant or linear map is a linear combination of these elements.

zh.text: 方法一：等变多项式的完整基，每个基元就是一个多重图
论文的第一个贡献，是给出了所有次数不超过 d 的等变图多项式的一组完整基。定理 2.1 说：这组基可以用有向多重图 H = (V, E, (a, b)) 来枚举，其中顶点数 |V| ≤ min{n, 2+2d}、边数 |E| ≤ d，(a, b) 是一条被标成红色的特殊边。换句话说，“等变多项式”这个抽象空间，被一一对应地翻译成了“一批小图”。
更关键的是，每个基元在图上怎么取值？答案是一次张量收缩，也就是深度学习里熟悉的 einsum：按 H 的每条黑边把邻接矩阵的元素相乘，再对内部节点求和。下面这张最简单的例子，就是我们再熟悉不过的矩阵乘法。

zh.caption: 图2 矩阵乘法 XY 作为一次张量收缩的例子：三个节点、两条黑边加一条红色输出边，对应的 einsum 恰好就是 (XY) 这个矩阵乘积。这说明作者所谓的“张量收缩”并不神秘，它就是把常见的图上线性代数运算统一写成了多重图的语言。

zh.text: 怎么保证这些多项式是等变的？作者用 Reynolds 算子（Reynolds operator）把普通的单项式在所有节点置换上做平均。论文进一步证明，这个平均恰好等于对 H 的轨道（orbit，即 H 在所有置换下得到的所有同构副本）求和。于是“构造一个等变多项式”这件事，被化简成了“枚举一个多重图的轨道”这件纯组合的事情。

zh.caption: 图3 常数（粗竖线左侧）与线性（粗竖线右侧）等变图多项式的完整基：每个格子里都是一个小多重图，红色边标出输出的位置。整张表就是低次等变多项式空间的一份“完整清单”，任何等变的常数或线性映射都是这些基元的线性组合。

en.title: A Finer Ruler for Graph Networks: Grade Them by the Polynomials They Compute
en.subtitle: An ICML 2023 paper from Weizmann, MIT, NVIDIA, and Meta gives a complete basis for equivariant graph polynomials, and uses it to build PPGN++, a new state of the art on molecular benchmarks.

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 换一把更细的尺子：用等变多项式衡量图神经网络的表达能力
zh.subtitle: Weizmann、MIT、NVIDIA 与 Meta 给出等变图多项式的完整基，并据此设计出刷新分子基准的 PPGN++

en.text: Contribution two: a linear-time test for a model's polynomial power

With a basis in hand, one can ask a very concrete question: given a GNN, which of these polynomials can it actually compute? The second contribution treats a network as a bank of primitive contractions F, and gives an algorithm (Algorithm 1) that decides, in time linear in |V| and |E|, whether a target polynomial can be assembled by repeatedly contracting nodes.

Applying this tool, the authors tabulate the polynomial power of standard GNNs, and two clean results fall out. A bank that only allows node contractions, F_n, turns out to equal 1-WL exactly; a stronger bank that also allows edge contractions, F_e, equals 2-FWL (better known as 3-WL). The figure below draws the primitive building blocks of both banks.

en.caption: Figure 4 (paper Figure 7). The prototypical node-based (left) and edge-based (right) contraction banks; gray nodes are the ones being contracted. The node-based bank F_n corresponds to 1-WL, and the edge-based bank F_e corresponds to 2-FWL (3-WL). The extra primitives on the edge side are precisely what make it stronger.

en.text: This is not a paper exercise. Table 1 quantifies it: on degree-3 polynomials the edge-based model F_e leaves only 0 of 18 basis elements non-computable, whereas the node-based F_n leaves 2 of 8, matching the fact that F_e is 5-node- and 4-edge-polynomial-exact while F_n reaches only 2-node-polynomial-exact.

zh.text: 方法二：一个线性时间算法，读出模型的“多项式功力”
有了基，就能问一个非常具体的问题：给定一个 GNN，它到底能算出上面哪些多项式？论文的第二个贡献，是把一个网络看成一“套”原始收缩操作（contraction bank）F，并给出一个在 |V|、|E| 上线性时间的算法（Algorithm 1），精确判定某个目标多项式能否被这套操作反复收缩组装出来。
用这套工具，作者把常见 GNN 的表达能力做成了一张对照表，并得到两个漂亮的结论：只允许“节点收缩”的操作集 F_n 恰好等价于 1-WL；允许“边收缩”的更强操作集 F_e 恰好等价于 2-FWL（也就是常说的 3-WL）。下图把这两套操作的原始积木画了出来。

zh.caption: 图4（论文 Figure 7）原型化的节点型（左）与边型（右）收缩操作库：灰色节点表示被收缩掉的节点。节点型操作库 F_n 对应 1-WL，边型操作库 F_e 对应 2-FWL（3-WL）。边型多出的几个积木，正是它比节点型更强的来源。

zh.text: 这张对照表不是纸面练习。论文的 Table 1 给出了量化：在 3 次多项式上，边型模型 F_e 只有 0/18 个基元算不出来，而节点型 F_n 有 2/8 个算不出来，直观印证了 F_e 是 5 节点、4 边多项式精确的，而 F_n 只到 2 节点多项式精确。

en.title: A Finer Ruler for Graph Networks: Grade Them by the Polynomials They Compute
en.subtitle: An ICML 2023 paper from Weizmann, MIT, NVIDIA, and Meta gives a complete basis for equivariant graph polynomials, and uses it to build PPGN++, a new state of the art on molecular benchmarks.

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 换一把更细的尺子：用等变多项式衡量图神经网络的表达能力
zh.subtitle: Weizmann、MIT、NVIDIA 与 Meta 给出等变图多项式的完整基，并据此设计出刷新分子基准的 PPGN++

en.text: Experiments: state of the art on molecules, past 3-WL on SR graphs

The evaluation spans two settings. For real-world performance, the authors use three standard molecular graph regression datasets: ZINC-12K (about twelve thousand molecules), the larger ZINC-full (over two hundred thousand), and Alchemy, all measured by test mean absolute error (MAE, lower is better), with every model held to a 500K parameter budget following Dwivedi et al. (2020) and Lim et al. (2022). For raw expressive power they use Strongly Regular (SR) graphs, families notoriously hard to tell apart that 3-WL cannot separate at all, measuring the failure rate at distinguishing non-isomorphic pairs.

en.caption: Table 1. Test MAE on three molecular graph regression benchmarks (lower is better, all within a 500K parameter budget). PPGN++ with degree-6 polynomial features is best in class on all three.

en.text: PPGN++ with degree-6 polynomial features takes the top spot on all three: 0.071 on ZINC-12K (versus 0.079 for CIN and 0.163 for GIN), 0.020 on ZINC-full, and 0.109 on Alchemy. Just as striking, the features are model-agnostic. Bolting degree-6 features onto a plain GatedGCN backbone cuts its ZINC-12K MAE from 0.265 to 0.106, so the benefit does not hinge on any one architecture.

Feature degree matters too, and monotonically. On ZINC-12K the base model scores 0.076, degree-5 features bring it to 0.072, and degree-6 to 0.071. On the SR graphs the same trend is far more dramatic.

en.caption: Figure 5 (paper Figure 10). Failure rate at distinguishing non-isomorphic SR graph pairs, by family (log scale, lower is better). For both the GatedGCN and PPGN backbones, adding polynomial features drives the failure rate down by orders of magnitude as the degree climbs from 5 to 7, while 3-WL fails on these graphs entirely. This is direct evidence that precomputed polynomial features push the model past the 3-WL barrier.

zh.text: 实验：分子基准全面刷新，SR 图上跨越 3-WL

作者在两类任务上验证。真实性能方面，用三个标准的分子图回归数据集：ZINC-12K（约一万二千个分子）、更大的 ZINC-full（二十多万个）和 Alchemy，指标是测试集平均绝对误差（MAE，越低越好），所有模型都严守 500K 参数预算，遵循 Dwivedi 等（2020）和 Lim 等（2022）的协议。表达能力方面，用强正则图（Strongly Regular graphs）这类出了名难区分、连 3-WL 都分不开的图，衡量区分非同构图对的失败率。

zh.caption: 表1 三个分子图回归基准上的测试集 MAE（越低越好，均在 500K 参数预算内）。带 degree-6 多项式特征的 PPGN++ 在三项上全部取得当前最好成绩。

zh.text: 三项基准的头名都由带 degree-6 多项式特征的 PPGN++ 拿下：ZINC-12K 上 0.071（对比 CIN 的 0.079、GIN 的 0.163），ZINC-full 上 0.020，Alchemy 上 0.109。更有意思的是，这些多项式特征是“即插即用”的：给一个普通的 GatedGCN 骨干加上 degree-6 特征，它在 ZINC-12K 上的 MAE 从 0.265 直接降到 0.106。也就是说，收益并不依赖某个特定架构。
特征的次数（degree）也确实越高越好。在 ZINC-12K 上，基础版为 0.076，加 degree-5 特征降到 0.072，加 degree-6 再降到 0.071，趋势单调。而在强正则图上，这个趋势更为剧烈。

zh.caption: 图5（论文 Figure 10）在各族强正则图上区分非同构图对的失败率（纵轴对数刻度，越低越好）。无论是 GatedGCN 还是 PPGN 骨干，一旦加入多项式特征，随着次数从 5 升到 7，失败率成数量级地下降；而 3-WL 本身对这些图完全无能为力。这直接印证了“预计算多项式特征把模型推过了 3-WL 屏障”。

The lasting contribution here is turning a vague question, "how expressive is this GNN?", into a concrete and checkable one: "which equivariant graph polynomials can it compute?" Every such polynomial is just a small multi-graph evaluated by a tensor contraction, which gives both a finer ruler than WL and an explicit, itemized list of exactly which operations a given model still lacks and could be extended to include.

Acting on that list, the authors use precomputed polynomial features to push ordinary graph networks past the 3-WL barrier and to state-of-the-art accuracy on molecular property prediction, all within a modest 500K parameter budget. It is worth being precise about the cost. Because the polynomial features are precomputed once, before training, and passed in as extra inputs, the gain in expressive power does not turn into a heavier per-step runtime, and every model reported in the paper still fits inside the same 500K parameter budget as its baselines. Paired with the linear-time computability algorithm, this is what lets the central question, whether a given network can compute a given polynomial, become something a practitioner can check directly and then act on, instead of a property that can only ever be argued about at the level of intuition and worst-case examples.

en.title: A Finer Ruler for Graph Networks: Grade Them by the Polynomials They Compute
en.subtitle: An ICML 2023 paper from Weizmann, MIT, NVIDIA, and Meta gives a complete basis for equivariant graph polynomials, and uses it to build PPGN++, a new state of the art on molecular benchmarks.

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 换一把更细的尺子：用等变多项式衡量图神经网络的表达能力
zh.subtitle: Weizmann、MIT、NVIDIA 与 Meta 给出等变图多项式的完整基，并据此设计出刷新分子基准的 PPGN++

en.caption: Figure 1. Two example basis elements of equivariant graph polynomials: node-valued (top) and edge-valued (bottom). Each basis element is a small directed multi-graph carrying one special (red) edge, and evaluating it on a graph is a single tensor contraction (an einsum). This is the paper's central intuition: a polynomial is just a small graph.

en.text: The problem: why WL is not enough

A GNN's expressive power is, at bottom, the set of functions of a graph it can represent, and that set is bounded: no matter how many layers you stack, a standard message-passing network cannot separate certain non-isomorphic graphs. WL characterizes this bound, but as noted it is neither constructive nor fine-grained. What the authors want instead is a ruler that both separates today's models and points directly at the operations a weak model is missing.

Earlier work had only characterized very low-degree equivariant maps, or leaned on WL, leaving a gap: a complete, computation-friendly description of what a GNN should be able to output. Filling that gap is the paper's starting point.

zh.caption: 图1 两个等变图多项式基元的例子：上方为节点值（node-valued），下方为边值（edge-valued）。每个基元都对应一个带一条红色特殊边的小多重图（multi-graph），在图上取值就等于按这个多重图做一次张量收缩（einsum）。这张图是全文的核心直觉：一个“多项式”其实就是一个小图。

zh.text: 小结：让“有多强”变成一个可检查、可执行的问题
这篇论文最持久的价值，是把一个含糊的问题“这个 GNN 有多强”变成了一个具体的问题“它能算出哪些等变图多项式”。每个这样的多项式都只是一个小多重图，取值就是一次张量收缩，于是我们既得到了一把比 WL 更细的尺子，也得到了一张“缺哪些运算”的清单。

顺着这张清单动手，作者用预计算的多项式特征把普通图网络推过了 3-WL 屏障，并在分子性质预测上取得了当前最好的精度，而这一切都在 500K 参数的适度预算内完成。作者也坦诚指出了后续方向，例如用一组“生成元”而非完整基来减少喂入网络的特征数量，以及把暂时不可计算的多项式作为层内的计算原语（而非预计算特征）来进一步提升表达能力。对做图学习的人来说，这项工作把“把模型改强”从玄学变成了一件有清单、可核对的工程。

en.title: A Finer Ruler for Graph Networks: Grade Them by the Polynomials They Compute
en.subtitle: An ICML 2023 paper from Weizmann, MIT, NVIDIA, and Meta gives a complete basis for equivariant graph polynomials, and uses it to build PPGN++, a new state of the art on molecular benchmarks.

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 换一把更细的尺子：用等变多项式衡量图神经网络的表达能力
zh.subtitle: Weizmann、MIT、NVIDIA 与 Meta 给出等变图多项式的完整基，并据此设计出刷新分子基准的 PPGN++

en.text: Contribution two: a linear-time test for a model's polynomial power

With a basis in hand, one can ask a very concrete question: given a GNN, which of these polynomials can it actually compute? The second contribution treats a network as a bank of primitive contractions F, and gives an algorithm (Algorithm 1) that decides, in time linear in |V| and |E|, whether a target polynomial can be assembled by repeatedly contracting nodes.

Applying this tool, the authors tabulate the polynomial power of standard GNNs, and two clean results fall out. A bank that only allows node contractions, F_n, turns out to equal 1-WL exactly; a stronger bank that also allows edge contractions, F_e, equals 2-FWL (better known as 3-WL). The figure below draws the primitive building blocks of both banks.

en.caption: Figure 4 (paper Figure 7). The prototypical node-based (left) and edge-based (right) contraction banks; gray nodes are the ones being contracted. The node-based bank F_n corresponds to 1-WL, and the edge-based bank F_e corresponds to 2-FWL (3-WL). The extra primitives on the edge side are precisely what make it stronger.

en.text: This is not a paper exercise. Table 1 quantifies it: on degree-3 polynomials the edge-based model F_e leaves only 0 of 18 basis elements non-computable, whereas the node-based F_n leaves 2 of 8, matching the fact that F_e is 5-node- and 4-edge-polynomial-exact while F_n reaches only 2-node-polynomial-exact.

zh.text: 方法二：一个线性时间算法，读出模型的“多项式功力”
有了基，就能问一个非常具体的问题：给定一个 GNN，它到底能算出上面哪些多项式？论文的第二个贡献，是把一个网络看成一“套”原始收缩操作（contraction bank）F，并给出一个在 |V|、|E| 上线性时间的算法（Algorithm 1），精确判定某个目标多项式能否被这套操作反复收缩组装出来。
用这套工具，作者把常见 GNN 的表达能力做成了一张对照表，并得到两个漂亮的结论：只允许“节点收缩”的操作集 F_n 恰好等价于 1-WL；允许“边收缩”的更强操作集 F_e 恰好等价于 2-FWL（也就是常说的 3-WL）。下图把这两套操作的原始积木画了出来。

zh.caption: 图4（论文 Figure 7）原型化的节点型（左）与边型（右）收缩操作库：灰色节点表示被收缩掉的节点。节点型操作库 F_n 对应 1-WL，边型操作库 F_e 对应 2-FWL（3-WL）。边型多出的几个积木，正是它比节点型更强的来源。

zh.text: 这张对照表不是纸面练习。论文的 Table 1 给出了量化：在 3 次多项式上，边型模型 F_e 只有 0/18 个基元算不出来，而节点型 F_n 有 2/8 个算不出来，直观印证了 F_e 是 5 节点、4 边多项式精确的，而 F_n 只到 2 节点多项式精确。

en.title: A Finer Ruler for Graph Networks: Grade Them by the Polynomials They Compute

zh.title: ICML 2023 | 换一把更细的尺子：用等变多项式衡量图神经网络的表达能力
zh.subtitle: Weizmann、MIT、NVIDIA 与 Meta 给出等变图多项式的完整基，并据此设计出刷新分子基准的 PPGN++

en.text: Contribution one: a complete basis, where every element is a multi-graph

The first contribution is a complete basis for all equivariant graph polynomials of degree at most d. Theorem 2.1 states that this basis is enumerated by directed multi-graphs H = (V, E, (a, b)), with |V| ≤ min{n, 2+2d}, |E| ≤ d, and (a, b) a marked (red) edge. In other words, the abstract space of equivariant polynomials is put into one-to-one correspondence with a collection of small graphs.

And how is each basis element evaluated on a graph? By a single tensor contraction, the einsum expression familiar from deep learning: multiply entries of the adjacency matrix along the black edges of H, then sum over the internal nodes. The simplest example of this is something everyone already knows: ordinary matrix multiplication.

en.caption: Figure 2. Matrix multiplication XY expressed as a tensor contraction: three nodes, two black edges, and one red output edge, whose einsum is exactly the product XY. The takeaway is that the paper's tensor contractions are nothing exotic; they are just familiar graph linear algebra rewritten in the language of multi-graphs.

en.text: How does the construction guarantee equivariance? The authors average an ordinary monomial over all node permutations using the Reynolds operator, and then show that this average equals a sum over the orbit of H, that is, over all the isomorphic copies of H obtained under permutation. Building an equivariant polynomial thus reduces to enumerating a multi-graph's orbit, a purely combinatorial task.

en.caption: Figure 3. The complete basis of constant (left of the bold line) and linear (right of the bold line) equivariant graph polynomials. Each cell is a small multi-graph, with the red edge marking the output slot. Together the grid is an exhaustive inventory of the low-degree space: every equivariant constant or linear map is a linear combination of these elements.

en.text: Takeaway: making "how expressive?" a checkable, actionable question

The lasting contribution here is turning a vague question, "how expressive is this GNN?", into a concrete and checkable one: "which equivariant graph polynomials can it compute?" Every such polynomial is just a small multi-graph evaluated by a tensor contraction, which gives both a finer ruler than WL and an explicit, itemized list of exactly which operations a given model still lacks and could be extended to include.

Acting on that list, the authors use precomputed polynomial features to push ordinary graph networks past the 3-WL barrier and to state-of-the-art accuracy on molecular property prediction, all within a modest 500K parameter budget. They are candid about what comes next, including working with a generating set of polynomials rather than the full basis to reduce how many features the network ingests, and incorporating currently-uncomputable polynomials as in-layer computational primitives rather than as precomputed features. For anyone working on graph learning, the paper turns "make the model stronger" from guesswork into a concrete engineering task with an actual checklist to work through.

It is worth being precise about the cost. Because the polynomial features are precomputed once, before training, and passed in as extra inputs, the gain in expressive power does not turn into a heavier per-step runtime, and every model reported in the paper still fits inside the same 500K parameter budget as its baselines. Paired with the linear-time computability algorithm, this is what lets the central question, whether a given network can compute a given polynomial, become something a practitioner can check directly and then act on, instead of a property that can only ever be argued about at the level of intuition and worst-case examples.
